title: Structure of the heart

2026-11-01T08:14:09Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank point covers the overall circulatory loop and blood vessel types, not the four heart chambers or the valves that keep blood flowing one way, so it is a different and broader idea.

draft.title: Structure of the heart
card: The heart is a muscular pump with four chambers. The two upper chambers are the atria. The two lower chambers are the ventricles.
receive blood coming into the heart. Blood from the body and from the lungs enters through them.
push blood out of the heart. The right ventricle sends blood to the lungs. The left ventricle sends it to the rest of the body.
Valves sit between the atria and ventricles, and at the exits from the ventricles. They open to let blood through and close to stop it flowing backwards, so blood moves one way.
draft.remember: Atria receive blood, ventricles pump it out, and valves keep it moving one way.

a.q: Which chamber of the heart pushes blood out to the whole body?
a.why: The left ventricle sends blood out to the rest of the body. The right ventricle is tempting because it also pumps blood out, but it sends blood only to the lungs.
a.clue: Pumping blood out is the job of a ventricle, and one side serves the body.

b.q: A runner in Geelong has a faulty valve between a ventricle and the artery leaving it. What is the most likely effect on blood flow?
opts: Some blood leaks backwards into the ventricle
Blood cannot enter the atria from the body
Blood flows faster because nothing blocks it
Blood moves to the lungs and skips the body
b.why: Valves close to stop blood flowing backwards. If one does not seal, some blood can leak back into the ventricle. Blood does not flow faster, because a valve that fails to seal makes the flow less one-way, not more efficient.
b.clue: What do valves stop blood from doing?

b.best: Some blood leaks backwards into the ventricle

check.summary: No problems found. The card is accurate and both questions have exactly one right answer: the left ventricle pumps blood to the body, and a faulty exit valve lets some blood leak back into the ventricle.
